_note: Fake /claim response for building the claim page before the real policy reader is ready. Matches maya_policy.pdf.

calculation.label: Age rule: oven is 6 years old, paid at 70%

covered_items: Oven repair or replacement after a sudden breakdown (heating element, motor, thermostat or control board)
excluded_items: Lost income while the oven is out (Business Interruption not purchased)
Spoiled stock caused by the breakdown (Spoilage not purchased)
Renting a temporary oven or kitchen (Rental Equipment not purchased)
required_documents: Repair estimate or replacement quote from a licensed technician
Technician's report on the cause of failure
Proof of purchase date (invoice or receipt)
Maintenance records for the last 12 months
Photos of the damage and serial number plate
deadline: Notify the insurer in writing within 30 days of the breakdown

source_clauses.quote: Age rule: equipment older than 5 years is paid at 70% of the repair or replacement cost.
Limit: we pay at most $4,000 for any one breakdown.
Lost income while equipment is being repaired or replaced (Business Interruption was not purchased).

claim_draft:
To: Maple Mutual Small Business Insurance, Claims Department
Re: Equipment Breakdown claim, Policy BSP-2025-0417

I am writing to notify you of an equipment breakdown at Maya's Bakery, 142 Dundas Street West, Toronto. On [date], our insured deck oven (Bakemaster DX-3, purchased June 2020) stopped heating and could not be repaired. A licensed technician has quoted $6,000 for replacement.

Under Section 2 of the policy (Equipment Breakdown Coverage), I am requesting payment for the replacement. I understand that, as the oven is over 5 years old, settlement is 70% of cost, subject to the $4,000 limit and the $500 deductible.

Enclosed: signed Proof of Loss form, technician's quote and report, original purchase invoice, maintenance records for the last 12 months, and photos of the oven and serial plate.

Please contact me at [phone/email] with any questions.

Sincerely,
Maya Rahman
